newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar closes firmer after weak U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar closes firmer after weak U.S. data.

text.p: * The Canadian dollar closed stronger on Friday at C$1.3490
(US$0.7413) from Thursday's close of C$1.3512 (US$0.7401) in
* The currency moved to the strong end of a tight range after
a report that U.S. January PPI was weaker than expected. *
Calm trading is expected before Tuesday's budget.
The Canadian dollar closed stronger on Friday at C$1.3490 (US$0.7413) from Thursday's close at C$1.3512 (US$0.7401) in light trading, dealers said.

They said the unit moved to the strong end of a tight trading range after a report that the U.S. January produce price index, a key measure of inflation, was weaker than expected. The index fell 0.3 percent in January.
Economists surveyed by Reuters had expected a 0.3 percent increase.
The report helped the Canadian dollar since it gave market players reason to hope for stable U.S. interest rates in March, dealers said.
Trading was quiet heading into a holiday weekend in the United States, traders said. Monday is President's Day and U.S. markets will be closed.

Market players are also sitting on their hands waiting for the Canadian federal budget next Tuesday, dealers said. While the currency market has already factored in most of the expected news from the budget, "things always happen anyway," said one trader.
On the crosses the Canadian dollar rose to 1.2507 marks from Thursday's close of 1.2453 marks and climbed to 92.11 yen from 91.92 yen.
